proof.text: All objects below are at the fixed finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$. The coefficient unit has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. The finite-stage preservation assertions of [prop-functor-package] therefore put $\omega_X=Ra_X^!A$, $D_XP=R\mathcal Hom_A(P,\omega_X)$, $G P=Rc_{1!}c_2^*P$ and $B=p_1^*Q\otimes_A^Lp_2^*D_XP$ in their respective bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. This last equality is [def-trf-external-product]. In particular $L\Delta^*B$ is in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, so the right-adjoint fixed-square comparison may be evaluated on it. Every exceptional functor here uses precisely the constructible admissibility required in the statement. The triangulated lifts in [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] give the same domain checks grade by grade for finite filtered inputs; the finitely many tensor/Hom summands remain in these domains.

source.place: §5.2.1(b); Lemma 5.3.2 proof, domains of the pre-evaluation factor

proof.text:
Apply [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] with $f=c_1$, $M=c_2^*P$ and $N=Q$, and invert its canonical comparison. Taking derived global sections gives
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GP,Q)\simeq R\Gamma(C,R\mathcal Hom_A(c_2^*P,c_1^!Q)).$$
Here [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model](2) identifies global sections of internal Hom with the global Hom complex, in both variables; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies $R\Gamma(X,Rc_{1*}(-))$ with $R\Gamma(C,-)$. Thus this is an isomorphism of complexes in the derived category of abelian groups, rather than merely the degree-zero adjunction bijection. The hypotheses of the tensor--Hom theorem hold by step 1 and the separated finite-type assumptions on $c_1$. Its comparison is natural in the two inputs and shift compatible.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, first displayed composite and the exceptional adjunction immediately following it; global sections version

proof.text:
The pullback compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies $c^*p_2^*P$ with $c_2^*P$; the exceptional compositor in [def-trf-admissibility] identifies $c^!p_1^!Q$ with $c_1^!Q$. The constant coefficient identifications compose because both maps send a constant section $a$ to the constant section $a$. Apply [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] with $M=p_2^*P$ and $N=p_1^!Q$, and then apply $c^!$ to the inverse of $\kappa_{Q,P}$ from [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier]. This gives
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(c_2^*P,c_1^!Q)\simeq c^!R\mathcal Hom_A(p_2^*P,p_1^!Q)\simeq c^!B.$$
The first argument is an ordinary pullback, as required by the exchange lemma. The exceptional hypotheses for the Künneth comparison are exactly those for $a_X$ and $p_1$ in the statement. Compose global sections of this comparison with step 2: the result is the specified $\alpha_{P,Q}$, with the inverse Künneth comparison in the required direction.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, construction of Tr″ using the external-duality identification, with the two legs interchanged

proof.text:
Let $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to R\Delta_*L\Delta^*$ be the ordinary adjunction unit. Apply $c^!$ and then $R\Gamma(C,-)$ to $\eta_B$. For $N=L\Delta^*B$, clause (2) of [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change] gives
$$c^!R\Delta_*N\xrightarrow{Bc}Ri_*d^!N.$$
After taking global sections, use the inverse direct-image compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $i:F\to C$ and global sections. We obtain the middle arrows of the asserted composite with target $R\Gamma(F,d^!L\Delta^*B)$. The ordinary unit and the composition transformations are among those specified in [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. In particular this uses the right-adjoint comparison $c^!R\Delta_*\to Ri_*d^!$, with exactly that orientation, and requires neither properness of $c$ nor a smoothness hypothesis on $\Delta$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, Tr″ before evaluation; §§5.2.1–5.2.2, ordinary unit and fixed-square exchange

proof.text:
By [def-trf-external-product], apply the monoidal comparison of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] to $\Delta$ and the two factors of $B$. Since $p_1\Delta=p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$, the inverses of the compositors of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] give
$$L\Delta^*B\simeq Q\otimes_A^LD_XP.$$
On flat K-flat representatives interchange homogeneous sections $u\in Q^a$, $v\in(D_XP)^b$ by $u\otimes v\mapsto(-1)^{ab}v\otimes u$. The tensor differential gives coefficients $(-1)^{ab}$ on $dv\otimes u$ and $(-1)^{ab+b}$ on $v\otimes du$ on either side, so this is a chain isomorphism, natural in both complexes, whose square is the identity. The resolving localization and natural-transformation descent in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] descend it to the signed symmetry of derived tensor. This yields $L\Delta^*B\simeq D_XP\otimes_A^LQ$. Apply $R\Gamma(F,d^!(-))$ to obtain the final arrow.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, target of Tr″, identifying diagonal restriction with dual tensor before ev

proof.text:
For $a:P'\to P$ and $b:Q\to Q'$, the map of external products is $b\boxtimes D_Xa:B(P,Q)\to B(P',Q')$. The adjunction comparison in step 2 and the exchange and Künneth comparisons in step 3 are natural in precisely these variables. Naturality of the unit says $(R\Delta_*L\Delta^*(b\boxtimes D_Xa))\eta_B=\eta_{B'}(b\boxtimes D_Xa)$; naturality of fixed-square exchange and the diagonal tensor comparison then gives
$$T''_{P',Q'}\circ R\operatorname{Hom}_X(Ga,b)=R\Gamma(F,d^!(D_Xa\otimes b))\circ T''_{P,Q}.$$
Thus the composite is contravariant in $P$ and covariant in $Q$. Its source and target are triangulated in each variable: use the triangulated operations and Hom/tensor lifts of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom], and then forget filtration (ordinary inputs may be placed in filtration degree zero). Contravariance uses the usual opposite triangulated structure; the tensor symmetry is the signed one of step 5.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.2 proof, assertion that Tr″ is a morphism of bifunctors; §§5.2.1–5.2.2

proof.text:
Use the filtered operations and compatible adjunction, composition and trace-construction transformations of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. Set $G^F=Rc_{1!}^Fc_2^{*F}$, $D_X^FP=R\mathcal Hom^F(P,\omega_X[0]_{\mathrm{fil}})$ and $B^F=Q\boxtimes^FD_X^FP$. For $P_p=\operatorname{gr}^pP$, $Q_q=\operatorname{gr}^qQ$, its tensor/Hom formulas give
$$\operatorname{gr}^rB^F=\bigoplus_{q-p=r}Q_q\boxtimes D_XP_p.$$
Indeed $\operatorname{gr}^{-p}D_X^FP=D_XP_p$, because $\omega_X$ has only grade zero. Form the filtered versions of the adjunction, exceptional-Hom exchange and Künneth maps used in steps 2–3 from these compatible transformations. On grade $r$ their maps are the finite direct sums over $q-p=r$ of the ordinary maps for $(P_p,Q_q)$, by the displayed Hom/tensor formulas and the graded compatibility clause. Each component is an isomorphism by steps 2–3, using [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom], [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] and [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier]. The graded pieces detect zero cones by [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom], so these filtered maps are isomorphisms and their inverses exist. Composing them in the same order defines $\alpha^F_{P,Q}:R\operatorname{Hom}^F_X(G^FP,Q)\simeq R\Gamma^F(C,c^{!F}B^F)$. Its underlying map is $\alpha_{\omega P,\omega Q}$. This verifies the inversions needed for the filtered construction rather than inferring invertibility from the underlying map alone.

source.place: §5.2.2, adjunction and inversion of filtered isomorphisms; Lemma 5.3.2 proof, bifunctor Tr″

proof.text: Continue with the filtered unit $\eta_{B^F}$ and filtered right-adjoint fixed-square exchange, followed by the filtered global direct-image compositor, all supplied by [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. The exchange has the type of [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change](2); its grade-$r$ map is that same comparison on $\operatorname{gr}^rL\Delta^*B^F$, hence is invertible by detection of zero cones. The filtered monoidal pullback/composition maps identify $L\Delta^{*F}B^F$ with $Q\otimes^FD_X^FP$. The signed swap of step 5 preserves the convolution filtration: a tensor of filtration degrees $u,v$ still has degree $u+v=v+u$ after the swap. It therefore defines the filtered signed symmetry, identifying the target with $D_X^FP\otimes^FQ$. The resulting composite is $T''^F$ with target $R\Gamma^F(F,d^{!F}(D_X^FP\otimes^FQ))$, where sections mean $R\operatorname{Hom}^F(A_F[0]_{\mathrm{fil}},-)$. Every constituent is natural in the two independent filtered inputs, so the naturality equation of step 6 holds with all functors filtered. Forgetting filtration respects every constituent, its inverse and their composition by the compatibility clause of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom]. Thus $\omega T''^F=T''$ under its specified source and target identifications. This proves the filtered and underlying assertions simultaneously.

title: Filtered pre-evaluation transformation for a correspondence
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $n\ge1$ and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to Z=X\times_sX$ an admissible correspondence of [def-trf-correspondence]. Use the constructible exceptional operations of [def-trf-admissibility] for $c$, both projections $p_1,p_2:Z\to X$, the diagonal $\Delta:X\to Z$, the structure maps $a_X:X\to s$, $a_F:F\to s$, and the fixed-square maps $i:F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)\to C$, $d:F\to X$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], so $ci=\Delta d$. Use the dual $D_XP=R\mathcal Hom_A(P,\omega_{X,A})$ of [def-trf-dualizing-complex], external products of [def-trf-external-product], and put $G=Rc_{1!}c_2^*$. For independent $P,Q\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let $B=Q\boxtimes_A^LD_XP$ and let $\alpha_{P,Q}$ be exceptional adjunction followed by the global sections of the canonical exceptional-Hom exchange of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] and $Rc^!\kappa_{Q,P}^{-1}$:
$$\alpha_{P,Q}:R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GP,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(C,Rc^!B).$$
Here $\kappa$ is the canonical comparison of [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier], with compositors identifying $c^*p_2^*=c_2^*$ and $c^!p_1^!=c_1^!$.
The composite
$$T''_{P,Q}:R\operatorname{Hom}_X(GP,Q)\xrightarrow{\alpha_{P,Q}}R\Gamma(C,Rc^!B)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(C,Rc^!R\Delta_*L\Delta^*B)\xrightarrow{Bc}R\Gamma(F,Rd^!L\Delta^*B)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(F,Rd^!(D_XP\otimes_A^LQ))$$
is a well-defined natural transformation, contravariant in $P$ and covariant in $Q$, between triangulated bifunctors. Its second arrow is induced by the ordinary adjunction unit, $Bc$ is the right-adjoint fixed-square base change of [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change](2) followed by the global direct-image compositor, and its final arrow is diagonal pullback followed by signed tensor symmetry. For $P,Q\in D^bF_{ctf}(X,A)$ of [def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category], with the filtered operations of [lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom] (equivalently transported from the small étale sites), the same composite defines a morphism of filtered bifunctors $T''^F$, whose underlying transformation is $T''$. Its target is $R\Gamma^F(F,Rd^!(D_X^FP\otimes_A^LQ))$, where $R\Gamma^F(T,-)=R\operatorname{Hom}^F_T(A_T,-)$ and $A_T,\omega_{X,A}$ are placed in filtration degree zero; $D_X^FP=R\mathcal Hom^F(P,\omega_{X,A})$.
